test.title: A festival or celebration in your country that you enjoy

document.cue: Describe a festival or celebration in your country that you enjoy.

text: The celebration I'd like to talk about is Nauryz, which marks the beginning of spring and the new year in Kazakhstan. It's celebrated around the twenty-second of March, when day and night are roughly the same length, and for most people it's a few days off work.

The best-known tradition is cooking nauryz kozhe, a special soup made from seven ingredients, including meat, milk and grains. Each ingredient symbolises something, like health or wealth, and families try to visit at least seven homes and taste the soup in each of them, which can be quite a challenge for your stomach.

In the cities, the main squares are filled with yurts, music and traditional games. Last year I went to the celebration in the central park with my younger brothers. We watched a kokpar match on a big screen, tried to win a prize at a strength contest, and ended up eating far too many baursaks.

I enjoy it because it feels genuinely joyful. Unlike some holidays, it isn't about expensive presents; it's about visiting people, forgiving old arguments and starting the new season with a clean slate. It's also one of the few days when you see people of every age and background celebrating together.
For me, Nauryz is the moment when winter finally feels over.
